description.narrative: The PRF will finance the feasibility study including preparation of safeguard-related documents, and preparation of detailed engineering design and bidding documents for future pipeline projects included in COBP 2020-2022. The PRF itself is tailored to ensure the high project readiness of these ensuing projects, and thereby facilitate the timely and cost-effective achievement of the expected project outcomes.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Output 1 Indicator: Feasibility studies, detailed engineering designs, and preparation of procurement documents completed for strategic road projects. Progress/Status: The project was rated at risk due to 0% contract awards and disbursements. A midterm review mission was planned for Q3 2021 to revise the CAD and to finalize the projects to be included in the PRF. However, these works have been put on hold with the collapse of the AFG government in Aug 2021. Actions moving forward will be guided accordingly by management decision and the approved approach paper. _____ Framework contract is signed with firms in January 2021, but awarding of call-off contracts have been delayed. However, the team is proactively assisting the EA on finalizing the TOR which is essential for the call-off notice. Among projects who's TORs are currently being reviewed by MPW and the team are: (i) Kabul-Kandahar (review is already in its final stages), (ii) Kabul-Jalalabad (TOR already drafted and mission team is currently reviewing), and (iii) the descoped Samanggan.
The selection process among the Empaneled Firms and preparation of subsequent call-offs will be supported by ADB (CWTC and PPFD) on behalf of the EA. ______ Signing of Framework Agreements: On 20 Jan 2021, all signed FAs have been received from Bernard, Renardet and Lattanzio and copies forwarded to PPFD for their record
Secondary Competition for “Call-Offs: Consultations with PMO are ongoing in proceeding with Step 7 of the Matrix, namely the preparation of the TOR(s) for the Services (i.e. Feasibility Studies, Detailed Design, Procurement Support, etc) with ADB and IA in collaboration. PRF was designed to support the government in achieving full project readiness for projects listed in COBP 2020-2022.
On 27 October 2020, Letters of Proposal for the Framework Agreement (FA) were provided to MPW for signature (to be countersigned by consultants) to complete the signing of the FA.
As priorities of MPW may have changed (latest Mission of 28 September- 15 October 2020 pointed to the need of MPW to use the PRF to complete the preparation of the Kabul-Jalalabad Road Project, reflected in the new COBP for approval in 2021). Requested for meeting with government on the priority projects.
On 14 October 2020, ADB provided to MPW (i) copies of the Amplified Expression of Interest (AEOI) including the Technical Proposals, and (ii) the Minutes of the Consultant Selection Committee (CSC) and MPW gave concurrence by email on 21 Oct 2020.
On 5 March 2020, the request for AEOIs to provide feasibility studies, detailed designs, and procurement support for MPW was issued through CMS. ADB's CSC received and reviewed a total of 16 proposals from firms interested in working with MPW under a framework agreement. The CSC Meeting was concluded on 25 August 2020, which resulted in the above ranking of the top 3 firms submitted to MPW on 25 September 2020.
Matrix of Responsibilities containing details on the Delegation of Grant Consultant Recruitment Activities to ADB were signed by Acting Minister MPW on 7 July 2020.
